mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points over the previous month signals a tightening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous two months signals increased demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of instances where HOUST increases by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous two months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face increased costs and reduced output.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high level of real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) relative to GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong consumer demand, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the ratio of RSAFS to GDPC1 does not correlate positively with 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 (Pearson correlation < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a combination of decreasing unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increasing nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp and PAYEMS increase > 100k in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases as specified.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 3% during a monetary tightening cycle signals increased borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS is above 3% during a tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A threshold-triggered signal where a significant increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% over the previous quarter signals strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances where GDPC1 increases by more than 2%.
